title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Control Assessment
framing: A control-by-control gap assessment against the NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5 security and privacy control catalog, suitable for enterprise IT and other information systems. This version covers the base controls only (control enhancements are a planned addition). The Low, Moderate and High baselines come from NIST SP 800-53B.
sourceNote: Control identifiers, titles and Low/Moderate/High baseline membership are transcribed from NIST SP 800-53B (Control Baselines for Information Systems and Organizations). The 20-family structure and the verbatim per-control 'Control:' statement text (all 300 base controls) are transcribed from NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5, Release 5.2.0; IA-13 (Identity Providers and Authorization Servers) and SA-24 (Design for Cyber Resiliency) were added in Release 5.2.0 and are not yet allocated to a baseline (assessable under the Full catalog profile); the control statement is shown in the 'What this control requires' expander on every control. Withdrawn controls and control enhancements are excluded from this version.
attribution: NIST Special Publications are works of the U.S. Government and are not subject to copyright in the United States. Sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (Release 5.2.0) and NIST SP 800-53B (National Institute of Standards and Technology).

gettingStarted.cardTitle: NIST SP 800-53 control assessment: how this instrument works
gettingStarted.intro: This is a control-by-control gap assessment against the NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 catalog (Release 5.2.0), for enterprise IT and other information systems. Each control is determined Satisfied or Other Than Satisfied, following the assessment model of NIST SP 800-53A. It is an alignment and gap tool, not a formal assessment or an authorization package.
bullets: The unit of capture is the control: 300 base controls across 20 families, grouped as Technical, Operational and Management.
Record each control as Satisfied or Other Than Satisfied: the binary determination used by SP 800-53A. Unknown reduces confidence; Not applicable drops the control.

The baseline above (Low, Moderate or High, from NIST SP 800-53B) sets which controls are expected. Choose Full catalog to assess every control with no baseline target. Program Management (PM) controls are expected in every baseline.

No single score is produced. The report is a profile of Satisfied / Other Than Satisfied counts by family, plus the roadmap of controls that are Other Than Satisfied. Control enhancements are out of scope in this version.

outcomes.controlText:
a. Enforce a limit of [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; and

outcomes.title: Concurrent Session Control
outcomes.controlText: Limit the number of concurrent sessions for each [Assignment: organization-defined account and/or account type] to [Assignment: organization-defined number].

a. Prevent further access to the system by [Selection (one or more): initiating a device lock after [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of inactivity; requiring the user to initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended]; and
